10	## 1. Problem Statement
11	
12	In a long tool loop on an Anthropic model, the prompt cache stops working. After about 18 to 22 messages, each request reads 0 cached tokens and writes the full prompt again. In session ffcf4115, requests 16 to 26 wrote 2.14 M tokens and read 0 (MEASURED, E1). Over all logged sessions, 234 of 2917 requests read 0 with a gap under 5 minutes (MEASURED, E7b).
13	
14	The cause is in our client, not in the provider:
15	
16	1. `stripStaleThinking()` (core, `agent/cache.ts`) removes the thinking blocks of every assistant message except the latest one, on every request. So the prompt of request N is never a prefix of request N+1. All 892 broken prefixes in 25 sessions start with a removed thinking block (MEASURED, E4).
17	2. The server looks for an older cache entry only within 20 positions before a breakpoint. A run of `tool_use` blocks or `tool_result` blocks counts as one position (DOC, E11). A model with exactly this rule and no fitted value predicts 97.3% of 2869 logged reads (MEASURED vs model, E8). When the last usable entry falls out of the window, every request reads 0.
18	3. We send only one rolling marker. Nothing keeps an entry inside the window.
19	
20	The strip has no proven reason:
21	
22	- It came from commit `eca98d7` (2026-05-30). The commit blames a 400 error on request size, on one session (d343a63d, 223 KB of signatures).
23	- The error text was "`thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified". That text is about a changed block, not about size.
24	- One hour earlier, commit `83d965a` fixed a real cause of that exact error: the SSE parser dropped `redacted_thinking` blocks. The original capture is lost (E15).
25	- The docs say that Fable 5.2, Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+ and Haiku 5.5 keep prior thinking by default. "You don't need to prune old thinking yourself". "Make your integration append-only" (DOC, E11, E16).
26	- Claude Code 2.1.325 re-sends old thinking: 16 of 23 assistant messages (MEASURED, E15).
27	
28	The fix was already built and measured: item C-30, commit `06b265f` on the local core branch `feat/cache-fixes`. Live A/B on Haiku 5.5 gave 14 → 0 breaks per session and -67.6% input cost (E16). It never reached main. The branch is local only and 286 commits behind main. An adversarial review (ADV-1) said "safe behind the flag only". It left one gate open: a live run past 250 KB of kept thinking. Nobody ran it.
29	
30	## 2. Solution
31	
32	1. Send each assistant turn back exactly as the API gave it (append-only), for Anthropic models that keep prior thinking. The prompt of request N is then a prefix of request N+1, and each request reads almost all of the previous prompt.

34	3. Count and cap the cache markers at 4 for each request.
35	4. Prove the change with one live long-loop run and the request-golden tests before it is the default.
